mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered months despite FEDFUNDS > 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% is associated with weakening household balance sheets, reducing equity demand and consumer confidence, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes where GDPC1 falls by >2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that rises above 4.0% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) is flat or declining indicates labor market softening, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals broad-based supply contraction, which raises input costs and dampens profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units, coinciding with a drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.5%, signals a housing demand shock in a low-inflation environment, which reduces construction-related equity exposure and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 1.2 AND CPIAUCSL < 2.5 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.75 percentage points within a quarter, without a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL, signals an emergency easing response to financial stress, which boosts risk appetite and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS quarterly change < -0.75% AND CPIAUCSL monthly change <= 0.1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 new jobs for four consecutive months, alongside an unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5%, signals a tight labor market that boosts wage growth and inflation, which ultimately pressures equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 for 4 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 3.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1.5% for two consecutive quarters indicates subpar economic momentum, which reduces corporate earnings and investor optimism, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10) in more than 40% of triggered quarters.
